newsitem.title: UK: Copper sits near $1,970 perch in late LME trading.
newsitem.headline: Copper sits near $1,970 perch in late LME trading.

text.p: Copper prices were reluctant to stray too far from the $1,970 level during Monday evening LME inter-office trading, marking time ahead of what should be another fall in warehouse stocks on Tuesday, traders said.
LME stocks are at six-year lows of 123,700 tonnes and are forecast to fall another 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes on Tuesday.
"Obviously, tomorrow's stock announcement will dictate in the short-term. It does appear as if the market has geared itself to another five-figure decline," one said.

Occasional forays towards the $2,000 level faltered, as there is not only Tuesday's inventory data to absorb, but also the November options declaration on Wednesday. The key strike prices are $1,950, $2,000 and $2,100, traders added.
Three month prices were indicated at $1,974/1,977 a tonne at 1900 GMT, against Friday's close of $1,958. The session peak remained at $1,985.
Aluminium prices edged up in the background - a move that reflected copper values. Prices were quoted at $1,427/1,429.
